values.value: You provided medical care in environments where equipment was limited and the margin for error was zero. You assessed patients fast, made treatment decisions independently, and worked under pressure without a full support team behind you. You have hands-on clinical experience that translates directly into patient care roles, and you understand what it means to operate in a high-stakes medical team.

[{"title": "Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) or Paramedic", "description": "You respond to medical emergencies, assess patients in the field, provide treatment, and transport people to the hospital. Combat medic and corpsman experience is a strong foundation; most states require a certification exam to practice.", "onet": "29-2042.00"}, {"title": "Surgical Technologist", "description": "You prepare operating rooms, assist surgeons during procedures, and handle instruments and equipment during surgery. The precision and sterile-field discipline required maps well to medic and corpsman training.", "onet": "29-2055.00"}, {"title": "Medical Assistant", "description": "You take patient histories, record vitals, assist with procedures, and handle clinical and administrative tasks in a doctor's office or clinic. This is often an entry point into civilian healthcare for those building toward additional credentials.", "onet": "31-9092.00"}, {"title": "Healthcare Administrator", "description": "You manage the operations of a clinic, hospital department, or healthcare facility, handling staffing, budgets, compliance, and scheduling. Military medical unit administrative experience is a direct match.", "onet": "11-9111.00"}, {"title": "Registered Nurse (RN)", "description": "You provide direct patient care, administer medications, monitor conditions, and coordinate with the care team. Military medics and corpsmen often pursue RN licensure through bridge programs designed for their background.", "onet": "29-1141.00"}]
